title: Have fun watching us bake a red velvet cake

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Okay Grandma, the camera's rolling. Just act natural, like we're just baking together.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Act natural? I'm always natural, Matthew. Why would I act? Is this some kind of performance?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: No, I mean don't look at the lens. Just talk to me like normal.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: But you just told me to talk to the camera. Now you don't want me to? Make up your mind.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Never mind. Let's just start. So today we're making red velvet cake from a box mix, right?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: From a box? I thought we were making it from scratch. You said you wanted to learn real baking.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I do, but the video needs to be under thirty minutes. Box mix is faster for the content.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Content? You're more worried about that phone than the cake. This isn't how I taught your mother.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: It's not a phone, it's a camera. And yes, the content matters. That's the whole point of doing this.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: The point should be making a good cake. Not performing for strangers on the internet.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Can we just start? Please? Preheat the oven to three-fifty.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I know how to preheat an oven, Matthew. I've been doing this since before you were born.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I know, I was just saying it for the... never mind. Do you have the mix ready?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: It's right here. One box of red velvet. Though I still say we should add real cocoa.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: The box says it already has cocoa. We don't need extra.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Box cocoa isn't real cocoa. But fine. You want fast, we'll do fast. Don't blame me if it's bland.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: It won't be bland. The frosting will cover it anyway.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Cover it? You want to cover the flavor? That's not baking, that's hiding mistakes.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: That's not what I meant. I meant the frosting complements the cake.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Complements, covers—sounds like the same thing to me. Where are the eggs?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Three eggs. Room temperature, like you always say.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: At least you remembered something. Crack them into this bowl. And don't get shell in it.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I know how to crack eggs, Grandma. I'm not five.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Then stop holding them like they might bite you. Tap the side, not the middle.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I did tap the side. See? Perfect.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: There's a piece of shell right there. In the bowl. Look.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Oh. I didn't see it. I'll get it out.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Use the shell itself to fish it out. Not your fingers. I told you that last time.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: You didn't tell me that. You told me to wash my hands.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I told you both. You just weren't listening because you were looking at that screen.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: The screen is how I see if we're in frame. It's part of filming.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Filming. Baking. Which one are we doing right now? Because I can't tell.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Both. That's the whole concept. Cooking with Grandma, remember?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I thought the concept was spending time together. Not putting on a show.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: We are spending time together. This is just how I like to spend it.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: By turning me into a character? I don't want to be a character, Matthew.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: You're not a character. You're my grandma. The audience loves you.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: The audience. Right. People I don't know judging my kitchen. Lovely.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Nobody's judging. They think you're charming.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Charming. Is that why you keep telling me to smile more? I'm not a doll.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I never said smile more. I said look up occasionally.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Same thing. You want me to perform. I'm here to bake.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Okay. Forget the camera. Just bake. I'll stay out of your way.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: You're not in my way. You're just... distracted. Pour the mix in.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Fine. Pouring the mix. One box of red velvet going in.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Slowly. Don't dump it. We want it aerated.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: It's a box mix. It doesn't need aerating. It's already processed.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Everything needs care. Even processed things. You treat it like garbage, it tastes like garbage.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I'm not treating it like garbage. I'm being efficient.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Efficient. That's your generation's word for careless.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Can we not make this about generations? It's just cake.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Just cake. To you, maybe. To me, it's memory. It's Sunday dinner. It's your grandfather's birthday.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I know. I'm sorry. I didn't mean to dismiss it.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Yes you did. But you don't know you did. That's the problem.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I do know. I just... I get caught up in the video. I want it to look good.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Why does it need to look good? It needs to taste good. The looking is for people who won't eat it.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: But the looking is what gets people to try it. That's how it works now.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: How what works? Life? Or entertainment?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Both, kind of. You need to hook people visually first.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Hook them. Like fish. That's what you think of people?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: It's just an expression. I don't literally think they're fish.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Expressions mean things. Words matter. Especially when you're teaching.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I'm not teaching. I'm sharing.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Sharing what? You haven't measured anything yet.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: The box says one cup of water. I'm measuring.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Use the liquid measure, not the dry cup. Look at you, using the one-cup scoop.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: What's the difference? A cup is a cup.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: No, it isn't. Dry and liquid measure differently. The volume is different.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Really? I thought cups were standardized.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Standardized by who? The box company? They want it to work, not be perfect.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Okay, liquid measure. Got it. One cup of water.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Not cold water. Room temperature. Cold shocks the batter.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: The box doesn't say that.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: The box doesn't say a lot of things. That's why you need me.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Yeah. I do need you. That's why I wanted to do this together.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Then stop fighting me on every step and just listen.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I'm not fighting. I'm asking questions. That's how I learn.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Questions are fine. Arguing is not. You asked, I answered. That should be the end.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: It is the end. I switched to the liquid measure. See?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Good. Now the oil. A third of a cup.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Vegetable oil? Or can I use coconut oil? It's healthier.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Coconut oil tastes like coconut. This is red velvet, not a tropical drink.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: But it's subtle. You won't even taste it.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I'll taste it. Trust me. Use neutral oil. Vegetable or canola.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Fine. Vegetable oil. Third of a cup.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Now the eggs. Beat them first, then add them.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: The box says add them whole. One at a time.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: And I say beat them first. They incorporate better. Less lumps.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: But the instructions—

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: The instructions are for people who don't know better. You know me. Do it my way.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Okay. Beating the eggs. Then adding them.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Gently. Don't overmix. Gluten will develop and it'll be tough.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: It's box mix. It's already got gluten inhibitors or something.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Inhibitors? Is that a real word or did you make it up?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: It's real. Some mixes have tenderizers.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Tenderizers. Like meat. We're making cake, not steak, Matthew.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I know. I'm just saying the science is different from scratch baking.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Science. Everything is science with you. What about instinct?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Instinct is just internalized science. You've baked so long you don't think about the chemistry.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I don't think about chemistry because I don't need to. I feel the batter. You should try feeling instead of thinking.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I do feel. I feel like this is taking forever and the battery is dying.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Then charge it. Or turn it off. The cake won't know the difference.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: The audience will know. If it dies mid-shot, I lose the whole take.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: The whole take. Like a movie. Is that what I am now? A scene?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: No. You're my grandma. The scene is the cake. You're the expert.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Expert. At least that's better than character. Hand me the whisk.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Actually, can I use the electric mixer? It's faster.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Faster isn't better. You'll whip too much air in. The cake will collapse.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Only if I use high speed. Low speed for thirty seconds, then medium.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Where did you read that?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Online. A baking blog. They tested it.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: A blog. Written by who? A child in their bedroom?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Written by a pastry chef. With credentials.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Credentials. Paper. I've got forty years of cakes. That's my credential.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I know. I'm not saying you're wrong. I'm saying there are multiple right ways.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Multiple right ways. Is that what they teach in school now? Everyone's right?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Not every way. But some ways are faster and give the same result.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Same result. You think a rushed cake and a careful cake taste the same?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I think Dad won't know the difference.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: He will. Not with his mouth, maybe. But with his eyes. And his heart.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: ...Okay. No chilling. We'll do it your way. All the way.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Don't pout. Pouting makes your hands shake. Shaky hands make wavy sides.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I'm not pouting. I'm concentrating.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: You're pouting. But you're mixing. That's something. Keep going. Figure-eight pattern.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Figure-eight? Why not circles?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Circles create a vortex. Air pockets. Figure-eight folds without trapping air.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: That's... actually useful information. Why didn't you say that before?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I did. You weren't listening. You were checking your battery.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Fair. I'm listening now. Figure-eight. Got it.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Good. Now, when it's smooth, stop. Don't keep going just because you're angry.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I'm not angry. I'm just... processing.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Processing. Another new word. In my day we just said thinking.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: It's the same thing.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: It isn't. Processing sounds like a machine. Thinking sounds like a person.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Maybe I'm part machine now. Phone in one hand, whisk in the other.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Then put the phone down and be human for twenty minutes. The cake needs you.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Okay. Phone down. Being human. Whisking.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Better. See? Your shoulders dropped. You were tense.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I was tense because I want this to be good. For you. For the video. For both.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: It will be good. If you stop wanting and start doing. Grease the pans.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: With butter or spray?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Butter. Always butter. Spray has chemicals.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: It's just oil and lecithin. Not chemicals.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Lecithin. Sounds like a chemical to me. Use butter.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Butter it is. Pans greased.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Dust them with flour too. Or the cake will stick.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: The box says non-stick pans don't need it.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Non-stick lies. Everything sticks if you don't respect it. Flour the pans.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Okay. Flouring the pans. Lots of flour.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Not lots. A light dusting. Tap out the excess. You want a coat, not a snowstorm.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Right. Light dusting. Tapping out.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Now pour the batter. Equal amounts in each pan. We want even layers.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Should I weigh them? For precision?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: You can eye it. You've got eyes, don't you?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I have eyes. But a scale would be more accurate.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Accuracy is for laboratories. Baking is about judgment. Split it evenly. Trust yourself.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Okay. Splitting by eye. Here goes.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Stop. That's too much in the left one. Scoop some out.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: They look even to me.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Then look harder. The left is higher by half a finger. Move some over.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Half a finger. Your finger or my finger?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: A finger is a finger. Don't be smart.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Moving batter. Left to right. Better?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Better. Now into the oven. Middle rack. Don't open the door for twenty minutes.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: What if I need to check?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: You don't need to check. Opening the door drops the temperature. The cake sinks.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Even for a second?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Even for a second. Patience. Something your generation could use more of.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: My generation has plenty of patience. We just use it differently.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Differently. Meaning not at all?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Meaning we wait for downloads, not ovens.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Downloads. Ovens. One feeds you, the other doesn't. Remember that.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I will. Twenty minutes. No peeking.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Good. Now we wait. And we talk. Without the camera, if you can manage.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I can manage. What do you want to talk about?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Tell me why you really wanted to do this. The truth, not the video answer.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: The truth? I miss spending time with you. And this was an excuse.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: An excuse. At least you're honest. I miss you too. Even when you're annoying.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I'm not annoying. I'm enthusiastic.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Enthusiastic. Annoying. Same thing from where I stand.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Fair. Is it ready yet?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: It's been four minutes. No.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: It smells good though.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: It does. That's the cocoa. Real or boxed, cocoa always smells like home.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Home. Yeah. This kitchen smells like home.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Then maybe put the phone down more often and just be here. Home doesn't need a director.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I'll try. No promises.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Trying is enough. For now.
